78187-the-quarterly-of-the-oregon-histor.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. The early Oregon pioneers not only gained the first secure foothold for the American people on the Pacific Coast, but their movement opened the way to American occupation and in itself counted as an occupation of that realm for American civilization. They moved across the continent at an auspicious time, and so were able to influence, if not to shape, the course of great events touching the widening of the American dominion on the Pacific.

arxiv-2108-13628.title: Learning Optimal Prescriptive Trees from Observational Data
arxiv-2108-13628.creator: Nathanael Jo, Sina Aghaei, Andrés Gómez, Phebe Vayanos
arxiv-2108-13628.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Nathanael Jo, Sina Aghaei, Andrés Gómez, Phebe Vayanos. We consider the problem of learning an optimal prescriptive tree (i.e., an interpretable treatment assignment policy in the form of a binary tree) of moderate depth, from observational data. This problem arises in numerous socially important domains such as public health and personalized medicine, where interpretable and data-driven interventions are sought based on data gathered in deployment – through passive collection of data – rather than from randomized trials.

arxiv-2208-14723.description: Abstract Membrane computing and P systems are a paradigm of massively parallel natural computing introduced by Gheorghe Păun in 1999, inspired by the structure of the living cell and by its biochemical reactions. arxiv-2507-21738.creator: Huiqiang Chen, Tianqing Zhu, Xin Yu, Wanlei Zhou
arxiv-2507-21738.description: Abstract Machine unlearning aims to remove the influence of specific samples from a trained model. A key challenge in this process is over-unlearning, where the model’s performance on the remaining data significantly drops due to the change in the model’s parameters. Existing unlearning algorithms depend on the remaining data to prevent this issue.

pmc-10646438.title: Recent advances in biopolymers-based carbon materials for supercapacitors
pmc-10646438.creator: Hongjie Li, Yanyu Li, Shenmin Zhu, Yulong Li, Imran Zada, Yao Li
pmc-10646438.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Supercapacitors as potential candidates for novel green energy storage devices demonstrate a promising future in promoting sustainable energy supply, but their development is impeded by limited energy density, which can be addressed by developing high-capacitance electrode materials with efforts. Carbon materials derived from biopolymers have received much attention for their abundant reserves and environmentally sustainable nature, rendering them ideal for supercapacitor electrodes.

pmc-10714247.title: An Unusual Presentation of Subscapularis Tendon Calcific Tendonitis
pmc-10714247.creator: Muath Alqahtani, Ahmed Jalal, Ahmad Alghamdi, Abdulrasheed Halawani, Mamdouh Masri
pmc-10714247.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Rotator cuff tendons are predisposed to calcific tendonitis and may present in single or multiple tendons. Despite the existence of several treatment strategies that have been proposed, clinical outcomes are controversial. Our study aims to report a case of large subscapularis tendon calcific tendonitis that was refractory to non-operative management and to investigate the clinical presentation, imaging findings, and treatment outcomes.

pmc-11860451.title: Sodium oxybate – new views on an old candidate This presentation will outline the outcome of a clinical development program, including a Phase 3 study, on sodium oxybate in the treatment of alcohol dependence
pmc-11860451.creator: J Guiraud
pmc-11860451.description: Abstract Sodium oxybate (SMO) has shown efficacy in the treatment of alcohol withdrawal syndrome (AWS) and in the maintenance of abstinence in alcohol dependent (AD) patients in a series of pilot randomized controlled trials. SMO is marketed in these indications in Italy and Austria since 1991 and 1999, respectively.

pmc-12461143.title: Kidney interstitial edema as the central pathophysiological mechanism of NSAKI: a call for reappraisal
pmc-12461143.creator: Osamu Uemura
pmc-12461143.description: e hallmark of nephrotic syndrome—hypoalbuminemia—leads to a decrease in plasma oncotic pressure. This shift promotes transcapillary fluid movement into the interstitium, causing generalized edema, including in the kidney interstitium. As kidney tissues become edematous, intrarenal pressure rises, compressing both glomerular and peritubular capillaries, leading to ischemia. Systemic hemodynamics may seem normal or overloaded, yet kidney perfusion remains low.

pmc-12467277.title: Proteomic Analysis of Antheraea pernyi Larvae After Injection of Vitamin C and Preliminary Exploration of the Function of Antheraea pernyi Aldonolactonase
pmc-12467277.creator: Xin Xu, Zhongwen Liu, Yongjun Zhang, Yaoting Zhang, Yanxian Lian, Zhen Zhang, Xuwei Zhu
pmc-12467277.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Simple SummaryVC (Vitamin C) is an essential substance for regulating the physiological functions of Antheraea pernyi and an important component in nutrients and artificial feed. We analyzed the midgut proteome of larvae injected with VC and used GO (Gene Ontology) functional annotation and KEGG (Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes) analysis to identify proteins related to the metabolism of VC in A. Then, we cloned the ApALase (Antheraea pernyi Aldonolactonase) gene and performed bioinformatic analysis.

pmc-13180768.creator: Yefeng Fan, Simon Richard White
pmc-13180768.description: Exponential random graph models (ERGMs) are flexible probabilistic frameworks to model statistical networks through a variety of network summary statistics. Conventional Bayesian estimation for ERGMs involves iteratively exchanging with an auxiliary variable due to the intractability of the ERGM likelihood. However, this approach has limited scalability in large-scale implementations.

pmc-13238928.title: Investigation of the Effects of Methylphenidate on Hemodynamic Parameters in Children With ADHD
pmc-13238928.creator: Caglar Charles Daniel Jaicks, Selman Vefa Yıldırım
pmc-13238928.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This prospective observational study investigated the acute effects of a single 10 mg dose of methylphenidate (MPH) on hemodynamic and electrocardiographic parameters in 60 children aged 6–16 years newly diagnosed with Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD). All participants received 10 mg short‐acting MPH, and systolic and diastolic blood pressure, heart rate, and electrocardiographic measurements (QTc, PR, QRS intervals, and rhythm) were obtained both before and 30–45 min after administration under standardized conditions and interpreted by a pediatric cardiologist.

pmc-13333636.title: Congenital Hypoglossia With Craniofacial Anomalies Without Limb Defects: A Rare Phenotypic Variant of Oromandibular–Limb Hypogenesis Syndrome
pmc-13333636.creator: Abraham Kwadzo Ahiakpa, Liza Georgina Agyapong‐Quaittoo, Emmanuella Haluri Ayeh, Precious Akosua Raphaelson, Dorothy Sackey
pmc-13333636.description: Congenital hypoglossia can present with life‐threatening airway compromise even in the absence of limb anomalies or classical syndromic features. Early airway assessment, feeding support, and timely referral from resource‐limited settings are critical for survival. Such cases may represent a broader phenotypic spectrum of oromandibular–limb hypogenesis syndrome.
